output.summary: KEP-4026 adds a batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp annotation to Jobs created by a CronJob, recording the original expected scheduled time. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
output.rationale: There was no supported way to get the original or expected scheduled timestamp for a Job created from a CronJob. The CronJob controller sets this value as a Job annotation. The design chose this approach so that adding the annotation would not disrupt existing workloads.

alternatives.option: Add a label instead of an annotation
alternatives.why_not: Labels are unnecessary because the data is not used with search or to satisfy conditions.
The object's CreationTimestamp would be overridden with the time the CronJob starts, so the original scheduled time would be lost; the new annotation is meant to carry that original/expected value.

evidence.quote: Currently, there is no supported way to get the original/expected initial scheduled timestamp for the job created from a cronjob.
Adding the annotation should not be disruptive to existing workloads.
Labels are unnecessary as we need to pass data that won't be used with search or satisfy certain conditions.
The object already has the `CreationTimestamp` field, but it will get overridden with the time the CronJob will start.
